text:
Marathon Petroleum is up 0.7% today, continuing a sharp nine-day rally that's pushed the stock up 9.6% since September 11th. The timing and magnitude of this move track closely with oil prices and refinery conditions: US crude has climbed to $107 a barrel, global oil hit $130.80, and refineries are running at 96.8% capacity—near maximum utilization. When refineries run hot like this and crude prices rise, refining margins (the profit spread between what a refiner buys crude for and what it sells gasoline and diesel for) tend to widen, which directly boosts earnings for a major refiner like Marathon.

The broader energy-market backdrop reinforces this. Geopolitical tension around the Middle East—fires near Saudi Arabia's main airport and ongoing Houthi attacks—has kept oil prices elevated despite initial fears that a Saudi pipeline outage would be more severe than it turned out to be. Record diesel prices in particular are creating strong demand and pricing power across the refining sector. All of this creates a favorable environment for refiner profitability right now.
